The two-depth violation test this row's own Method section asks for is therefore, by the dispatch's own logic, a test that the EXISTING data path (already proven honest and correct by G-125) survives being reached through a NEW orchestration layer unchanged -- not a re-proof of the drainage model itself.

twoFloodsDistinction.decision: The mount opens in its own frame (the existing 'map' MountStage, taken to Full), REPLACING the city's own Leaflet/SmartSite map view for the duration -- never rendered simultaneously with the city's own FEMA-zone layer. Inside that frame, PE's own map already colour-separates FEMA (muted blue, labelled 'reference') from the derived study (slate-teal hydro family), per the pre-existing Legend in FloodTool.tsx (not changed by this row). This row adds one explicit words-not-colour banner at the top of the report inside the embed, because a colour-only distinction is not enough for a screen a staff member may view once.
twoFloodsDistinction.bannerTextVerbatim: Two different questions: this is a MODELED drainage study of what happens when it rains, not the regulatory FEMA flood zone. A parcel can sit entirely outside the FEMA zone and still be modeled here to pond badly — that is not a contradiction, it is the case this study exists to catch. This result does not change the parcel's FEMA determination.
twoFloodsDistinction.bannerLocation: apps/property-explorer/src/workbench/tools/FloodTool.tsx, FLOOD_VS_FEMA_EMBED_BANNER constant, data-testid="flood-vs-fema-banner", rendered at the top of FloodDrainageSection only when isFloodDrainageEmbedRequest(window.location.search) is true (i.e. only inside this row's mount, never for a normal signed-in PE consumer viewing the same report).

honestyStringVerbatim.mechanism: This row's mount renders FloodDrainageSection UNCHANGED for every honesty-critical string -- it is not re-derived, re-formatted, or composed by this row's own code; the only additions are the banner above it and a 'still working' progress line during a poll, both clearly separate from the study's own reported facts.
honestyStringVerbatim.screenDisclaimerVerbatim: Screening-level drainage model, not a drainage study or engineering determination. Verify drainage with a licensed engineer before design or permitting. (FLOOD_DRAINAGE_SCREEN_DISCLAIMER, floodDrainageClient.ts -- rendered on-screen in both the modeled-result and honest-empty states, per G-125.)
honestyStringVerbatim.designStormLineVerbatim: Design storm 4 inch, 24-hr. -- G-125's own live production verification (2026-09-14, revision hauska-engine-api-00224-joq, parcel 48021:34049, a 4-inch parameter-sourced run) after PR #447 fixed a live-caught fabrication (the pre-fix string falsely read 'Design storm 4 inch, 100-yr 24-hr', inventing a return period). This row did not re-run that exact call (no signed-in session available this row -- see leave_behind); it is cited because this row's mount reaches the identical rendering code (drainage-gradient.ts buildGradientNote, unchanged) through an unchanged request contract, so the same honest string is what the mount would render for the same input.
honestyStringVerbatim.runningLinePreparingVerbatim: Still working — the first run on this parcel can take a couple of minutes on a cold start. This will update on its own; no need to retry. (FLOOD_RUNNING_LINE_PREPARING, this row's own new copy, shown only during the poll fallback -- never claims a result that has not arrived.)

cacheMissAndTimeoutDetermination: NOT a cache-miss issue and NOT depth-specific, per G-125's own live measurement (cited and not re-derived here): flood-drainage has no refresh-level caching at any depth, and the dominant cold-run cost (92.5-102.8s measured) is container/subprocess cold start, not the rainfall parameter.
